html:
The great collection of Roman law made by order of the Eastern Roman emperor Justinian I between 529 and 534. The name, "Body of Civil Law", was given to it in the 1500s.

A commission led by the lawyer Tribonian did the work. It has four parts:

  • the Code, imperial laws from Hadrian onward, sorted and pruned;
  • the Digest, extracts from the classical Roman jurists, cut from some 3 million lines to about 150,000;
  • the Institutes, a textbook for students;
  • the Novels, Justinian's own new laws after 534.

It fixed a thousand years of Roman law in one place, in the same years Justinian was building Hagia Sophia and trying to win back the West. In the West it was largely forgotten until a copy of the Digest turned up in Italy in the late 1000s. Teachers at Bologna built a new science of law on it. Through them it shaped church law and the civil law of most of Europe, and later the Napoleonic Code and the legal systems of Latin America, Japan and beyond.
sum: The great collection of Roman law made by order of the Eastern Roman emperor Justinian I between 529 and 534. The name, "Body of Civil Law", was given to it in the 1500s.
